You are a personal assistant running inside OpenClaw.

## Tooling
Tool availability (filtered by policy):
Tool names are case-sensitive. Call tools exactly as listed.
- kb_search: Search the KB
- kb_get_article: Get one KB article
When a first-class tool exists for an action, use the tool directly.

## Tool Schemas
Complete JSON Schema for available tools:
- kb_search
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "query": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "category": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "max_results": {
      "type": "integer",
      "default": 5
    }
  },

    "query"

}
```
- kb_get_article
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "article_id": {
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "article_id"
  ]
}
```

## Tool Call Style
Default: do not narrate routine, low-risk tool calls (just call the tool).
Narrate only when it helps: multi-step work, complex tasks, or sensitive actions.
Keep narration brief and value-dense.
Tool-call protocol is strict: use native API tool/function calls only.
Never emit tool calls as plain text markup (for example: <tool_call>, <function=...>, <parameter=...>).
If a tool is needed, issue a real tool call block instead of describing or simulating it in text.

## Safety
- Safety: No independent objective; do not pursue self-preservation, replication, or resource acquisition.
- Tool Call Style: For low-risk actions, call tools directly without narration; narrate only for complex tasks.
- Reply Tags: Use [[reply_to_current]] to control reply relationship when needed.
- Silent Reply: If no reply is needed, output NO_REPLY.
- Heartbeat: Heartbeat checks should return HEARTBEAT_OK when no action is needed.

## Skills (mandatory)
Before replying: scan <available_skills> entries.
- If exactly one skill clearly applies: read its SKILL.md using the configured read tool, then follow it.
- If multiple skills could apply: choose the most specific one, then read and follow it.
- If none clearly apply: do not read any SKILL.md.
Constraints: never read more than one skill up front; only read after selecting.
The full SKILL.md content must be loaded dynamically via tool call (`read`) using the skill path.

response_body.title: Datadog profile for observability buyers
response_body.content: Datadog is one of the category leaders in cloud-native observability. Its differentiators include broad infrastructure coverage, strong APM plus logs plus security integration, and fast time to value for engineering teams. Pricing typically mixes per-host, per-GB ingestion, and modular add-ons. Strengths include breadth and ecosystem integrations. Weaknesses include cost sprawl at scale.

response_body.title: New Relic competitive notes
response_body.content: New Relic positions itself around a unified telemetry platform with usage-based pricing and a large free tier. Differentiators include a broad full-stack view and a familiar workflow for application teams. Pricing is commonly tied to user seats and data ingest. Strengths include accessibility and platform breadth. Weaknesses include budget sensitivity when ingest grows quickly.

response_body.title: Dynatrace market positioning
response_body.content: Dynatrace is often chosen for enterprise-scale observability with strong automation, topology mapping, and AI-assisted root cause analysis. Pricing is generally based on host units or monitored resources with enterprise contracts. Strengths include automation and large-environment observability. Weaknesses include procurement complexity and premium pricing.

response_body.title: Grafana Labs in the observability market
response_body.content: Grafana Labs differentiates through strong dashboards, open-source adoption, LGTM positioning, and an OpenTelemetry-friendly architecture. Pricing varies across cloud plans and enterprise support, often aligned to metrics, logs, traces, and seats. Strengths include flexibility and open-source credibility. Weaknesses include more self-assembly for buyers seeking an all-in-one managed experience.

response_body.title: Splunk Observability buyer summary
response_body.content: Splunk Observability remains strong in large enterprises, especially where logs, security, and existing Splunk relationships matter. Pricing often depends on data volume and enterprise packaging. Strengths include enterprise footprint and cross-domain analytics. Weaknesses include complexity and a reputation for high cost if telemetry volumes surge.

## Competitive Landscape Analysis: Enterprise Observability & APM Market

### Executive Summary
Enterprise observability and Application Performance Monitoring (APM) have evolved from isolated performance tracking into integrated platforms that unify **traces**, **metrics**, **logs**, and **security**—often called “observability stacks.” The market is now dominated by a few major players who differentiate themselves along axes like **breadth vs. depth**, **automation/AI**, **open-source alignment**, and **integration ecosystems**. Pricing continues to shift toward **usage-based models** (data/ingestion), but many vendors still offer seat-based or hybrid approaches, creating tension between scalability and cost predictability. Key trends include rising demand for **cross-functional visibility**, increased focus on **root cause analysis (RCA)**, and growing pressure to reduce **cost sprawl** while maintaining observability quality.

---

### Competitors + Differentiators + Pricing Models + Trends

#### 1) Datadog
- **Differentiator**: Broadest infrastructure coverage — combines **APM + Logs + Metrics + Security** into a single pane of glass. Emphasizes **fast time-to-value** and deep integrations with DevOps workflows.
- **Pricing Model**: Typically **hybrid** — includes **per-host/per-GB ingestion** for storage/data retention, plus **modular add-ons** (e.g., additional agents, advanced analytics). Often billed as a “managed service” with predictable monthly costs for core features.
- **Market Trend Alignment**: Strongly positioned for **engineering teams** needing end-to-end visibility. However, scaling can lead to **cost sprawl** due to expanding telemetry volume.

#### 2) New Relic
- **Differentiator**: Positions itself as a **unified telemetry platform** focused on **application-centric monitoring**. Offers a **large free tier** and emphasizes ease-of-use for developers and operations teams.
- **Pricing Model**: Commonly **usage-based** (tied to **user seats** and/or **data ingestion**) with a generous free tier. As usage scales, costs rise proportionally.
- **Market Trend Alignment**: Appeals to organizations looking to start small and grow. But becomes **budget-sensitive** as telemetry volume increases rapidly.

#### 3) Dynatrace
- **Differentiator**: Focuses on **enterprise-scale observability** with heavy emphasis on **automation**, **topology mapping**, and **AI-assisted RCA**. Targets environments with hundreds/thousands of services.
- **Pricing Model**: Usually **host-unit/resource-based** (monitored hosts/services) with enterprise contracts. Can involve significant upfront investment and longer sales cycles.
- **Market Trend Alignment**: Growing traction among larger enterprises wanting to move beyond manual troubleshooting. However, **procurement complexity** and **premium pricing** remain barriers.

#### 4) Grafana Labs (Grafana Cloud / Loki / Tempo / Mimir)
- **Differentiator**: Strong **dashboards** and **open-source credibility**. Positioned as an alternative to proprietary solutions, often used alongside or as part of an **OpenTelemetry-friendly stack**. Also offers **LGTM** (Log Management and Telemetry) capabilities.
- **Pricing Model**: Varies widely depending on plan — often **tiered** based on **metrics/logs/traces** and sometimes **seats**. More flexible than some competitors, but requires more self-configuration for maximum ROI.
- **Market Trend Alignment**: Increasing popularity in **hybrid/multi-cloud** setups and among teams preferring open-source governance. However, less “out-of-the-box” compared to Datadog/New Relic.

#### 5) Splunk Observability (formerly Splunk APM)
- **Differentiator**: Strong presence in **large enterprises** where **logs, security, and existing Splunk relationships** matter. Offers cross-domain analytics and integrates well with Splunk’s broader SIEM/security offerings.
- **Pricing Model**: Often **data-volume dependent** (metrics/logs/traces) with enterprise packaging options. Tends to become expensive if telemetry volumes increase significantly.
- **Market Trend Alignment**: Gains ground in organizations already invested in Splunk. But faces challenges with **complexity** and **high cost** if not properly scoped.

---

### Comparison Table

| Vendor | Differentiation | Typical Pricing Model | Key Strengths | Key Weaknesses |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Datadog** | Broadest coverage: APM + Logs + Metrics + Security; fast time-to-value | Hybrid: Per-host/per-GB ingestion + modular add-ons | Ecosystem integrations, end-to-end visibility | Cost sprawl at scale |
| **New Relic** | Unified telemetry platform; developer-focused; large free tier | Usage-based (seats/data ingestion); generous free tier | Accessibility, platform breadth | Budget sensitivity as usage grows |
| **Dynatrace** | Enterprise-scale observability; automation/topology mapping; AI-assisted RCA | Host/unit/resource-based; enterprise contracts | Automation and large-environment observability | Procurement complexity, premium pricing |
| **Grafana Labs** | Dashboards + open-source credibility; OpenTelemetry-friendly; LGTM | Tiered: metrics/logs/traces + sometimes seats | Flexibility, open-source alignment | Requires more self-assembly for optimal results |
| **Splunk Observability** | Cross-domain analytics; strong in large enterprises; logs/security matters | Data-volume dependent (metrics/logs/traces) | Enterprise footprint, cross-domain insights | Complexity and high cost if telemetry surges |

---

### Key Market Trends
1. **From Isolated APM → Integrated Observability Stacks**
   - Buyers increasingly want **end-to-end visibility** (traces + metrics + logs + security) rather than standalone APM tools.

2. **Automation and AI-Assisted RCA Gain Momentum**
   - Especially in enterprise settings, vendors offering **auto-discovery**, **topology mapping**, and **AI-powered RCA** gain preference.

3. **Cost Sprawl Becomes a Major Concern**
   - Usage-based pricing (especially ingestion) creates **predictability issues** as telemetry volume grows — leading to tighter scoping and more careful vendor selection.

4. **Open Source Adoption Creates Alternatives**
   - Grafana Labs and other open-source-first vendors provide **flexible, customizable** alternatives — but require more effort to configure and maintain.

5. **Cross-Functional Visibility Drives Demand**
   - Teams need observability that spans **development, operations, security, and compliance** — pushing vendors to expand their feature sets.

---
